problem:
The quadratic polynomial $P(x)$ has roots ${x}_{1}=2,{x}_{2}=-5,$ and the coefficient of the quadratic term is $-3.$ Find $P(x).$

$P(x)=$ {{field-1}}
worked_solution:
Since our quadratic polynomial has roots ${x}_{1}=2$ and ${x}_{2}=-5,$ and the coefficient of the quadratic term is $a=-3,$ we can write the polynomial as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}a(x-{x}_{1})(x-{x}_{2}) & =(-3)(x-2)(x-(-5)) \\  & =-3(x-2)(x+5)\end{aligned}
$$

Expanding the parentheses, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}-3(x-2)(x+5) & =-3({x}^{2}+5x-2x-10) \\  & =-3({x}^{2}+3x-10) \\  & =-3{x}^{2}-9x+30.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $P(x)=-3{x}^{2}-9x+30.$
